verses.zh: 这事以后，又有一事。耶斯列人拿伯在耶斯列有一个葡萄园，靠近撒马利亚王亚哈的宫。
verses.en: After this the following episode took place.[NOTE:1] Naboth the Jezreelite owned a vineyard in Jezreel adjacent to the palace of King Ahab of Samaria.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “after these things.” The words “the following episode took place” are added for stylistic reasons.
For location see Map2-B1; Map4-D3; Map5-E2; Map6-A4; Map7-C1.sn King Ahab of Samaria. Samaria, as the capital of the northern kingdom, here stands for the nation of Israel.

verses.zh: 亚哈对拿伯说：「你将你的葡萄园给我作菜园，因为是靠近我的宫；我就把更好的葡萄园换给你，或是你要银子，我就按着价值给你。」
verses.en: Ahab said to Naboth, “Give me your vineyard so I can make a vegetable garden out of it, for it is adjacent to my palace. I will give you an even better vineyard in its place, or if you prefer,[NOTE:1] I will pay you silver for it.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “if it is good in your eyes.”
The Old Greek translation includes the following words: “And it will be mine as a garden of herbs.”

verses.zh: 拿伯对亚哈说：「我敬畏耶和华，万不敢将我先人留下的产业给你。」
verses.en: But Naboth replied to Ahab, “The Lord forbid that I should sell you my ancestral inheritance.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Far be it from me, by the Lord, that I should give the inheritance of my fathers to you.”

verses.zh: 亚哈因耶斯列人拿伯说「我不敢将我先人留下的产业给你」，就闷闷不乐地回宫，躺在床上，转脸向内，也不吃饭。
verses.en: So Ahab went into his palace, bitter and angry that Naboth the Jezreelite had said,[NOTE:1] “I will not sell to you my ancestral inheritance.”[NOTE:2] He lay down on his bed, pouted,[NOTE:3] and would not eat.
notes: Heb “on account of the word that Naboth the Jezreelite spoke to him and he said.”
Heb “I will not give to you the inheritance of my fathers.”
Heb “turned away his face.”

verses.zh: 王后耶洗别来问他说：「你为甚么心里这样忧闷，不吃饭呢？」
verses.en: Then his wife Jezebel came in and said to him, “Why do you have a bitter attitude and refuse to eat?”

verses.zh: 他回答说：「因我向耶斯列人拿伯说：『你将你的葡萄园给我，我给你价银，或是你愿意，我就把别的葡萄园换给你』；他却说：『我不将我的葡萄园给你。』」
verses.en: He answered her, “While I was talking to Naboth the Jezreelite, I said to him, ‘Sell me your vineyard for silver, or if you prefer, I will give you another vineyard in its place.’ But he said, ‘I will not sell you my vineyard.’”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “While I was talking…, I said…, he said….” Ahab’s explanation is one lengthy sentence in the Hebrew text, which is divided in the English translation for stylistic reasons.

verses.zh: 王后耶洗别对亚哈说：「你现在是治理以色列国不是？只管起来，心里畅畅快快地吃饭，我必将耶斯列人拿伯的葡萄园给你。」
verses.en: His wife Jezebel said to him, “You are the king of Israel![NOTE:1] Get up, eat some food, and have a good time.[NOTE:2] I will get the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite for you.”
notes: Heb “You, now, you are exercising kingship over Israel.”
Heb “so your heart [i.e., disposition] might be well.”

verses.zh: 于是托亚哈的名写信，用王的印印上，送给那些与拿伯同城居住的长老贵胄。
verses.en: She wrote out orders,[NOTE:1] signed Ahab’s name to them,[NOTE:2] and sealed them with his seal. She then sent the orders[NOTE:3] to the leaders[NOTE:4] and to the nobles who lived in Naboth’s city.[NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “scrolls.”
Heb “in the name of Ahab.”
Heb “scrolls.”
Heb “elders.”
Heb “to the nobles who were in his city, the ones who lived with Naboth.”

verses.zh: 信上写着说：「你们当宣告禁食，叫拿伯坐在民间的高位上，
verses.en: This is what she wrote:[NOTE:1] “Observe a time of fasting and seat Naboth in front of the people.
notes: Heb “she wrote on the scrolls, saying.”

verses.zh: 又叫两个匪徒坐在拿伯对面，作见证告他说：『你谤渎　神和王了』；随后就把他拉出去用石头打死。」
verses.en: Also seat two villains opposite him and have them testify, ‘You cursed God and the king.’ Then take him out and stone him to death.”

verses.zh: 那些与拿伯同城居住的长老贵胄得了耶洗别的信，就照信而行，
verses.en: The men of the[NOTE:1] city, the leaders,[NOTE:2] and the nobles who lived there[NOTE:3] followed the written orders Jezebel had sent them.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “his.”
Heb “elders.”
Heb “and the nobles who were living in his city.”
Heb “did as Jezebel sent to them, just as was written in the scrolls which she sent to them.”

verses.zh: 宣告禁食，叫拿伯坐在民间的高位上。
verses.en: They observed a time of fasting and put Naboth in front of the people.

verses.zh: 有两个匪徒来，坐在拿伯的对面，当着众民作见证告他说：「拿伯谤渎　神和王了！」众人就把他拉到城外，用石头打死。
verses.en: The two villains arrived and sat opposite him. Then the villains testified against Naboth right before the people, saying, “Naboth cursed God and the king.” So they dragged him[NOTE:1] outside the city and stoned him to death.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “led him.”
Heb “and they stoned him with stones and he died.”

verses.zh: 于是打发人去见耶洗别，说：「拿伯被石头打死了。」
verses.en: Then they reported to Jezebel, “Naboth has been stoned to death.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Naboth was stoned and he died.” So also in v. 15.

verses.zh: 耶洗别听见拿伯被石头打死，就对亚哈说：「你起来得耶斯列人拿伯不肯为价银给你的葡萄园吧！现在他已经死了。」
verses.en: When Jezebel heard that Naboth had been stoned to death, she[NOTE:1] said to Ahab, “Get up, take possession of the vineyard Naboth the Jezreelite refused to sell you for silver, for Naboth is no longer alive; he’s dead.”
notes: Heb “Jezebel”; the proper name has been replaced by the pronoun (“she”) in the translation for stylistic reasons.

verses.zh: 亚哈听见拿伯死了，就起来，下去要得耶斯列人拿伯的葡萄园。
verses.en: When Ahab heard that Naboth was dead,[NOTE:1] he got up and went down to take possession of the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite.
notes: The Old Greek translation includes the following words here: “he tore his garments and put on sackcloth. After these things.”

verses.zh: 耶和华的话临到提斯比人以利亚说：
verses.en: The Lord’s message came to Elijah the Tishbite:

verses.zh: 「你起来，去见住撒马利亚的以色列王亚哈，他下去要得拿伯的葡萄园，现今正在那园里。
verses.en: “Get up, go down and meet King Ahab of Israel who lives in Samaria. He is at the vineyard of Naboth; he has gone down there to take possession of it.

verses.zh: 你要对他说：『耶和华如此说：你杀了人，又得他的产业吗？』又要对他说：『耶和华如此说：狗在何处舔拿伯的血，也必在何处舔你的血。』」
verses.en: Say to him, ‘This is what the Lord has said: “Haven’t you committed murder and taken possession of the property of the deceased?”’[NOTE:1] Then say to him, ‘This is what the Lord has said: “In the spot where dogs licked up Naboth’s blood they will also lick up your blood—yes, yours!”’”
notes: The words “of the property of the deceased” are supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.

verses.zh: 亚哈对以利亚说：「我仇敌啊，你找到我吗？」他回答说：「我找到你了；因为你卖了自己，行耶和华眼中看为恶的事。
verses.en: When Elijah arrived, Ahab said to him,[NOTE:1] “So, you have found me, my enemy!” Elijah[NOTE:2] replied, “I have found you, because you are committed[NOTE:3] to doing evil in the sight of[NOTE:4] the Lord.
notes: Heb “and Ahab said to Elijah.” The narrative is elliptical and streamlined. The words “when Elijah arrived” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
Heb “he”; the referent (Elijah) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “you have sold yourself.”
Heb “in the eyes of.”

verses.zh: 耶和华说：『我必使灾祸临到你，将你除尽。凡属你的男丁，无论困住的、自由的，都从以色列中剪除。
verses.en: The Lord says,[NOTE:1] ‘Look, I am ready to bring disaster[NOTE:2] on you. I will destroy you[NOTE:3] and cut off every last male belonging to Ahab in Israel, including even the weak and incapacitated.[NOTE:4]
notes: The introductory formula “the Lord says” is omitted in the Hebrew text, but supplied in the translation for clarification.

Disaster. There is a wordplay in the Hebrew text. The word translated “disaster” (רָעָה, raʿah) is similar to the word translated “evil” (v. 20, הָרַע, haraʿ). Ahab’s sins would receive an appropriate punishment.
Heb “I will burn after you.” Some take the verb בָּעַר (baʿar) to mean here “sweep away.” See the discussion of this verb in the notes at 14:10 and 16:3.

Heb “and I will cut off from Ahab those who urinate against a wall, [including both those who are] restrained and let free [or “abandoned”] in Israel.” The precise meaning of the idiomatic phrase עָצוּר וְעָזוּב (ʿatsur veʿazuv, translated here “weak and incapacitated”) is uncertain. For various options see HALOT 871 s.v. עצר and M. Cogan and H. Tadmor, II Kings (AB), 107. The two terms are usually taken as polar opposites (“slaves and freemen” or “minors and adults”), but Cogan and Tadmor, on the basis of contextual considerations (note the usage with אֶפֶס (ʾefes), “nothing but”) in Deut 32:36 and 2 Kgs 14:26, argue convincingly that the terms are synonyms, meaning “restrained and abandoned,” and refer to incapable or incapacitated individuals.

verses.zh: 我必使你的家像尼八的儿子耶罗波安的家，又像亚希雅的儿子巴沙的家；因为你惹我发怒，又使以色列人陷在罪里。』
verses.en: I will make your dynasty[NOTE:1] like those of Jeroboam son of Nebat and Baasha son of Ahijah because you angered me and made Israel sin.’[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “house.”
Heb “because of the provocation by which you angered [me], and you caused Israel to sin.”

verses.zh: 论到耶洗别，耶和华也说：『狗在耶斯列的外郭必吃耶洗别的肉。
verses.en: The Lord says this about Jezebel, ‘Dogs will devour Jezebel by the outer wall[NOTE:1] of Jezreel.’
notes: A few Hebrew mss and some ancient versions agree with 2 Kgs 9:10, 36, which reads, “the plot [of ground] at Jezreel.” The Hebrew words translated “outer wall” (חֵל, khel, defectively written here!) and “plot [of ground]” (חֵלֶק, kheleq) are spelled similarly.

verses.zh: 凡属亚哈的人，死在城中的必被狗吃，死在田野的必被空中的鸟吃。』」
verses.en: As for Ahab’s family, dogs will eat the ones[NOTE:1] who die in the city, and the birds of the sky will eat the ones who die in the country.”
notes: “Dogs will eat the ones who belonging to Ahab who die in the city.”

verses.zh: （从来没有像亚哈的，因他自卖，行耶和华眼中看为恶的事，受了王后耶洗别的耸动；
verses.en: (There had never been anyone like Ahab, who was firmly committed[NOTE:1] to doing evil in the sight of[NOTE:2] the Lord, urged on by his wife Jezebel.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “who sold himself.”
Heb “in the eyes of.”
Heb “like Ahab…whom his wife Jezebel incited.”

verses.zh: 就照耶和华在以色列人面前所赶出的亚摩利人，行了最可憎恶的事，信从偶像。）
verses.en: He was so wicked he worshiped the disgusting idols,[NOTE:1] just as the Amorites[NOTE:2] whom the Lord had driven out from before the Israelites.)
notes: The Hebrew word used here, גִלּוּלִים (gillulim) is always used as a disdainful reference to idols. It is generally thought to have originally referred to “dung pellets” (cf. KBL 183 s.v. גִלּוּלִים). It is only one of several terms used in this way, such as אֱלִילִים (ʾelilim, “worthless things”) and הֲבָלִים (havalim, “vanities” or “empty winds”).
Heb “He acted very abominably by walking after the disgusting idols, according to all which the Amorites had done.”

verses.zh: 亚哈听见这话，就撕裂衣服，禁食，身穿麻布，睡卧也穿着麻布，并且缓缓而行。
verses.en: When Ahab heard these words, he tore his clothes, put on sackcloth, and fasted. He slept in sackcloth and walked around dejected.

verses.zh: 耶和华的话临到提斯比人以利亚说：
verses.en: The Lord’s message came to Elijah the Tishbite,

verses.zh: 「亚哈在我面前这样自卑，你看见了吗？因他在我面前自卑，他还在世的时候，我不降这祸；到他儿子的时候，我必降这祸与他的家。」
verses.en: “Have you noticed how Ahab shows remorse[NOTE:1] before me? Because he shows remorse before me, I will not bring disaster on his dynasty during his lifetime, but during the reign of his son.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “humbles himself.” The expression occurs a second time later in this verse.
Heb “I will not bring the disaster during his days, [but] in the days of his son I will bring the disaster on his house.”
